title: AIVTuber Shadow Divergence Report
description: Aggregated active-vs-shadow divergence evidence for exactly one compatibility identity (issue #165). Evidence only: it records how often two policies disagreed under a stated identity and carries no field that could promote a shadow policy to active behaviour. Case references are runtime identifiers, never payload or generated text.

orchestration.description: The bounded-orchestration identity the caller supplied and the aggregator validated. Copied verbatim from the input; never reconstructed from a current constant, because a report must not claim bounds it cannot vouch for.

total_comparisons.description: Every record in the batch, including records whose shadow evaluation produced nothing or whose target pair was not comparable. An empty batch is refused rather than reported as zero divergence.

comparable_comparisons.description: Records that could actually be compared. This is the divergence-rate denominator; `shadow_unusable` and `target_incomparable` are excluded so neither a broken nor an unevidenced shadow policy can depress the rate.

diverged_comparisons.description: Comparable records where the two policies disagreed. Never exceeds comparable_comparisons.

category_counts.description: Count per divergence category. Every category is present, including zeroes, so two reports compare field by field.

fallback_vs_success.description: Exactly one side carries a fallback reason; the other is a clean success.

fallback_reason_mismatch.description: Both sides carry a fallback reason and the reasons differ (Timeout vs Unavailable). Distinct from fallback_vs_success, where only one side degraded.

shadow_unusable.description: Shadow evaluations with no usable decision. A failure to compare, never an agreement.

target_incomparable.description: Route classes matched but the runtime declined to compare the targets (for example two Generated routes, whose content is not retained). An absent comparison, never an agreement.

metrics.description: Flat #58-shaped metric map. Names follow the benchmark convention: `shadow.divergence.<category>_count` plus `shadow.divergence.rate_pct`.

divergent_cases.description: References for offline review sampling. Runtime identifiers only: there is no field that can hold payload or generated text.

divergent_cases_truncated.description: True when divergent_cases holds fewer references than diverged_comparisons. Counts are never truncated, so totals stay honest.

orchestration.description: Bounded-orchestration identity the batch was produced under (#164). Two batches differing only in deadline, sample rate, concurrency, queue capacity or provider-call/budget flags are not comparable even under an identical policy identity.

bounds_fingerprint.description: Stable fingerprint over the orchestration bounds, so two batches can be compared only when they were collected the same way.

compatibility.description: The identity every record in this report shares. `ShadowPolicyIdentity` defines a dataset id per side, so both are held separately: two batches whose active datasets differ are incompatible even when the shadow dataset matches.

case_ref.description: A runtime handle for replay, never content.

category.description: Only diverging categories appear here; agreement and the two non-comparable categories are aggregations, not reviewable divergences.

allOf.description: A reviewable reference is always a disagreement, so it is never agreement nor one of the two non-comparable categories.
